result.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
result.summary: Work on debugging LLM agents treats the "first mistake" marked by a human or LLM judge as ground truth for where a trajectory failed. We ask whether such labels point at causes or symptoms, and make the distinction executable: we restart the agent from reconstructed intermediate states of a failed trajectory and estimate its prefix value V(h_t), the probability of success from each step, with a certified point of no return (PNR) for a failure. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, we build such curves for 47 and 60 failed trajectories and probe every step labeled by four frontier judges under the Traverse rubric. We find that the labels do not mark what a controller needs. Judges of different lineages agree on the exact step in only 21/57 cases, and the newest judges flag mistakes in 8/10 and 10/10 successful runs. For 66% of the labels, the agent's success probability does not drop at the labeled step; only 7/188 answers name the decisive step. Restarting at the measured restart point raises expected success from 0.44 to 0.57 offline, and real restarts confirm the advantage, whereas restarting at a judge's label does not (-0.08 to -0.03). We release our code, curves, and labels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验 LLM agent 失败轨迹中人／LLM 判官标注的「首个错误」究竟指向原因还是症状：从重建的中间状态重启 agent，估计每步成功率（前缀价值 V(h_t)）及失败的「不可逆点」，并在 SWE-bench Verified 的 150 个任务上比较按测量重启点与按判官标注重启的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其前缀价值曲线与重启验证提供了估计推理步骤因果贡献、定位决定性步骤的方法线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 步骤的贡献分配与停止决策；「判官标注不落在成功概率下降处」的发现也提示对 latent 轨迹监督信号的谨慎。
